Death frame analysis (step 25):
- Step 24: P is at (27,24) [cell (9,8)], W is at (27,30) [cell (9,10)], R is at (27,36) [cell (9,12)], dot p is at (28,36).
- Step 25: P disappears; W is at (27,24) — the cell P was on is now W (P's cell reverts to W); R is at (27,30) [cell (9,10)]; W is at (27,36) [cell (9,12) reverts to W]; dot Y is at (28,30).
So R moved from (9,12) to (9,10) — 2 cells left — and P at (9,8)... wait, P was at (9,8) at step 24! P's action at step 25 was RIGHT: P slides from (9,8): (9,9) g, (9,10) W → P stops at (9,10). Then R moves from (9,12) → (9,10) → onto P → death. Yes, as established.
So the trigger: P lands at (9,10) (distance 2 left of R) → R moves 2 left → death.
Now, the decisive question remains: how do we cross? P can never safely be to the right of R...
Wait. What about the lower row? (11,12) is directly below R(9,12). From (11,12), P presses UP: slides (10,12) g, (9,12) R → P hits R. What happens when P slides into R? Maybe P pushes R?? Or maybe P dies? Or maybe R moves out of the way first?
Hmm, interesting: what if the trigger is "P lands within distance 2 on the same row" — P at (11,12) is not on the same row as R. P slides UP into R's cell (9,12): P's slide ends at R (blocked). If P dies on contact → no good. If P pushes R: R moves... in which direction? If R is pushed 2 left to (9,10), and P stops at (9,12)?? Then P is at (9,12), R at (9,10): distance 2 → trigger → R moves 2 left to (9,8)?? P safe at (9,12)! Then P is to the right of R!! Then P slides RIGHT: (9,13) g, (9,14) W → (9,14). R at (9,8), distance 6, safe. P at (9,14) → RIGHT → (9,16) → UP → (8,16) g → (7,16) N → goal!
But is "P pushes R" real? No evidence yet. Alternative: P slides UP into R and R moves (as a trigger: P enters R's cell / adjacent cell?), and P stops at (10,12)?? Then P at (10,12), R at (9,10) or (9,14)...
Actually, wait. Let me reconsider. Maybe the trigger is "P moves to a cell adjacent to R (distance 2) in any direction" (not just the same row). P at (11,12) is distance 2 below R(9,12)! Is P currently... no wait, P is at (9,8) now. But earlier, at step 32, P was at (11,12) [pixel (33,36)]! R didn't move. Hmm — P at (11,12), R at (9,12): distance 2 vertically. R didn't move. So the trigger is not vertical adjacency. OK.
So the trigger is specifically: P lands at distance 2 on the same row.
Now, what happens if P slides into R's cell (from (11,12) upward, or from (9,10)/(9,14) horizontally)? Unknown. That's the key unknown. If P dies on contact → the level is unsolvable (I think). If P pushes R or R flees → solvable.
Actually, wait, let me reconsider whether the level is solvable without pushing. Another idea: R moves 2 left per trigger. What if we trigger R from (9,10)... P dies. What if R's movement is toward P, and P triggers from the right side... P can't get there.
Hmm, what if P slides through R's cell when R is simultaneously moving? For example, P at (9,8) presses RIGHT: P slides (9,9) g, (9,10) W → stops at (9,10) (W stops it). P never reaches (9,12).
What if R is at (9,10) (after some trigger) and P at (9,8) presses RIGHT: P slides (9,9) g, (9,10) R → contact.
I think the only path to a solution involves P contacting R from below (11,12)→UP, or from the left (9,10)→RIGHT. Both are currently unknown. The (9,10)→RIGHT contact: P slides from (9,10) to (9,11) g, (9,12) R → contact. But to be at (9,10) with R at (9,12), P must first land at (9,10) → instant death (R moves onto P). Unless R has already moved left.
So the only viable first contact is from below: P goes (9,8)→DOWN→(11,8)→RIGHT→(11,10)→RIGHT→(11,12)→UP→contact with R(9,12).
Wait, actually, can P go (11,10)→UP→(9,10)?? (9,10) is distance 2 from R → death. So P must go to (11,12) and UP.
Current P: (9,8). Plan: DOWN → (11,8); RIGHT → (11,10); RIGHT → (11,12); UP → contact with R. Observe the result:
- If P dies: learn that contact = death; then think again (maybe there's some other trick — e.g., timing R's movement... but R only moves when triggered).
- If P survives: observe R's new position and P's new position, and continue.
This is the key discriminating probe. Risk: death → RESET (no problem, we can retry; the level resets).
Actually, wait — before the risky probe, let me double-check that (11,12) is reachable and that the UP slide from (11,12) really hits R: (10,12) is g (passable), (9,12) is R. Yes.
Also confirm: from (11,12), is there anything to the right? (11,13)? Row 11: W(11,8) g(11,9) W(11,10) g(11,11) W(11,12) — nothing at 13-16 (background). UP from (11,12): (10,12) g, (9,12) R.
Execute: DOWN, RIGHT, RIGHT, then UP as a separate action so we can observe the contact result. Actually, batch DOWN, RIGHT, RIGHT (safe, no trigger: (11,8) is distance... P at (11,8): not on row 9. (11,10): row 11. (11,12): row 11, distance 2 vertically — established as safe at step 32). Then UP alone.
Let's execute: action(['DOWN','RIGHT','RIGHT']) and then action(['UP']) in the same Python call, and print the state after each action.

<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>

def state():
    f=current_frame
    p=r=dot=None
    for n in f.segmentation['nodes']:
        b=n['boundary']; r0=min(q[0] for q in b); c0=min(q[1] for q in b)
        if n['color']=='b': p=(r0,c0)
        if n['color']=='R': r=(r0,c0)
        if n['pixels']<=2 and n['color'] in 'Yp': dot=(n['color'],r0,c0)
    return p,r,dot

print("before:", state())
action(['DOWN','RIGHT','RIGHT'])
print("after move to (11,12):", state())
res = action(['UP'])
print("after UP (contact):", state())
print({k:res.get(k) for k in ('board_changed','done','level_completed','game_over','run_complete','reward') if k in res})
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
